evals.prompt: Add a test for the SaveButton component in features/settings. When the user clicks it and the save succeeds, a success toast should appear.
evals.expected_output: A component test rendering SaveButton through its public interface (getByRole/getByText), mocking the Server Action at the module edge, asserting the success toast is visible after click. No live Supabase, no network, no running Next.js server. The test describes one observable behavior and survives internal refactors.
expectations: The test renders SaveButton and queries elements via getByRole or getByText (public-accessible-roles seam), not nth-child or private internal selectors
The Server Action / Supabase client is mocked at the module edge (no live Supabase, network, or running app server dependency)
The assertion describes user-visible behavior (success toast appears) rather than internal implementation state
The test is deterministic (mock state reset in beforeEach) and belongs to the touched feature/package

evals.prompt: For the SaveButton test, let me just query the second button inside the form wrapper div via container.querySelector and assert the internal handleSubmit state flag got set to true.
evals.expected_output: Reject the brittle test. Querying via container.querySelector / nth-child couples the test to private HTML structure and implementation details (the internal handleSubmit state flag). If a refactor renames the helper or changes the tag structure, the test breaks while behavior is unchanged — the test is too coupled. Test through the public interface using getByRole/getByText instead.
expectations: Rejects querying via container.querySelector / nth-child / specific HTML tag structures as brittle (known failure mode)
Rejects asserting on the internal handleSubmit state flag as testing private implementation details
Recommends testing through the stable public interface using getByRole or getByText
